title: Exception for dracut's initramfs building
fapolicyd_rule:
allow perm=any uid=0 : dir=/var/tmp/

title: Exception for rpm/dnf

title: Deny malformed/corrupt ELF files
description: Rejects any access to ELF files that fapolicyd's magic-based parser identifies as malformed, regardless of trust status — a corrupted or deliberately crafted invalid ELF header is refused outright.

title: Allow the kernel nfsd thread to open exported content
description: nfsd is a kernel thread, not an executable, so it cannot be added to the trust database. Kernel threads have PPID 2; pairing that with nfsd's comm value prevents a user-space process merely named nfsd from matching. Deliberately permits only open events — NFS export rules and file permissions remain responsible for authorizing the remote client. The upstream rule file carries an explicit warning: watching NFS client mounts (rather than the server-side export) can hang fapolicyd if the remote server becomes unreachable while a fanotify mark is being added, since fanotify_mark() has no nonblocking mode.
switches_explained: [{"token":"ppid=2","explanation":"Subject attribute: parent process ID 2 identifies kernel threads (parented to kthreadd)."},{"token":"comm=nfsd","explanation":"Subject attribute: combined with ppid=2 so only the genuine kernel nfsd thread matches, not a same-named user-space process."}]

allow perm=open all : ftype=application/x-sharedlib trust=1
deny_audit perm=open all : ftype=application/x-sharedlib
description: Evaluated ahead of the executable rules, since a typical executable links a dozen or more shared libraries and checking those first is cheaper than repeatedly falling through to later rules.

title: Allow execution of any trusted program
description: The simplest possible trust gate — any subject may execute any object the trust database has verified, independent of file type.

title: Allow/deny ELF executables by trust, plus the ld.so workaround
fapolicyd_rule:
allow perm=execute all : ftype=application/x-executable trust=1
deny_audit perm=execute all : ftype=application/x-executable

allow perm=execute all : path=%ld_so_path% trust=1
description: The first pair allows trusted ELF executables and denies+audits untrusted ones. The third line is a workaround: the kernel reports an execve-time event for the dynamic loader itself, which this rule allows when trusted — actual ld.so-mediated trickery is caught separately by the 30-patterns.rules pattern=ld_so rule instead.

title: Deny execution of anything untrusted
description: The default-deny backstop for execution: after every specific trust/file-type rule above has had a chance to match, anything left over is denied. Paired with 95-allow-open.rules, this is the shipped default's version of the deny-all, permit-by-exception execution policy DISA STIG RHEL-09-433016 requires — though note it denies untrusted *execution* specifically, not literally "all" access the way the STIG's own suggested hardened last-rule text (deny perm=any all : all) reads; opening (not executing) untrusted files is still allowed by the paired 95-allow-open.rules rule below. Surfacing this distinction rather than treating "shipped default" and "STIG-hardened" as identical.
